slice.target: Cargo target.<triple>.<links> override portability and completeness limits
slice.finding: Cargo documents build-script override under target.<triple>.<links>, not target.<cfg>.<links>, so the documented override is target-triple-specific and portability requires supplying equivalent entries for each target triple that needs the override. The override can predeclare rustc-link-lib, rustc-link-search, rustc-flags, rustc-cfg, rustc-env, rustc-cdylib-link-arg and arbitrary links metadata. Cargo explicitly says warning, rerun-if-changed and rerun-if-env-changed should not be used in the override and are ignored. The documented override table does not provide keys for rustc-check-cfg or the generic/per-target-category rustc-link-arg variants (rustc-link-arg, rustc-link-arg-bin, rustc-link-arg-bins, rustc-link-arg-tests, rustc-link-arg-examples, rustc-link-arg-benches). Independently, build scripts may create files or intermediate artifacts in OUT_DIR and are used for native compilation, library discovery and code generation; a metadata-only links override does not itself create those artifacts.
slice.verified_scope: Current official Cargo Book documentation for Configuration and Build Scripts, including the target.<triple>.<links> override table, recognized build-script instructions, ignored override keys, and OUT_DIR/build-script side effects. No Cargo execution and no specific crate tested.
slice.not_verified_scope: Whether undocumented override keys are rejected versus treated as metadata in every Cargo version; specific-crate correctness without its build script; native/generated artifact availability; build-dependency pruning; cross-version behavior; actual compilation or end-to-end richer-mode parity.

sources.claim: The documented build-script override is target.<triple>.<links> and lists the supported predeclared values.
Cargo says the links override prevents the build script from being compiled or run, supplies metadata ahead of time, and ignores warning/rerun-if-changed/rerun-if-env-changed keys.
Build scripts can create OUT_DIR artifacts and Cargo recognizes additional instructions beyond those exposed by the override table.

scope_guard: Do not generalize the documented target-triple override into proof that a single portable entry covers all targets, that arbitrary build-script instructions are representable, or that native/code-generated artifacts can be replaced by metadata alone.
exact_continuation: On the next invocation, fresh-bootstrap and SHA-only validate current authority, then run one bounded official-source leaf on build-dependency behavior when a links build script is overridden: determine from Cargo source/docs whether the build script and its build-dependencies are omitted from the unit graph/compilation or merely the script execution is suppressed. Keep specific-crate correctness, native/generated artifact creation and actual compilation unresolved; do not run Cargo or start a second leaf.
